chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The recognition — from whose making is it?' He said: 'From the making of God. There is no making for the servants in it.'

key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةُ: al-ma'rifa — divine recognition, gnosis, or spiritual knowledge of God; a technical term in Islamic mysticism and Shia theology denoting the direct, experiential knowledge of God
key_terms.صُنْع: sun' — making, act of creation, craftsmanship; implies causation and intentional production

ai.seo_question: In Shia Islam, is the recognition of God (ma'rifa) from God's making or from human effort?
ai.summary: This hadith records a direct question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the origin of divine recognition (al-ma'rifa). The Imam's answer is unequivocal: gnosis and recognition of God are entirely from God's own making, with no contribution from the servants themselves. This teaching addresses a fundamental question in Shia theology — whether humans can achieve true knowledge of God through their own intellect or effort — and the Imam's response affirms divine monism: God alone is the author of the recognition by which He is known.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Hakeym who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The recognition (الْمَعْرِفَةُ) from a maker, whose is it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the Making of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. There isn’t for the servants, a making with regards to it’.
